details.title: Sign Out
details.definition: A sign-out invalidates the refresh token of the current session and blacklists the current access token until its natural expiry.

details.title: Sign Out
details.definition: The local session data and the stored tokens must always be cleared on the client, even when the server-side invalidation cannot be completed.

details.title: Reset Password
details.definition: A password reset code is single-use and expires 15 minutes after it is issued; a consumed or expired code is always refused.

details.definition: A scheduling request requires a destination, a travel date range and at least one interest tag.

details.title: Update Tour Package
details.definition: The departure date must not be earlier than the current date and the return date must not be earlier than the departure date.

details.title: Create Scheduling Request
details.definition: The trip duration of a single scheduling request must not exceed 30 days.

rules.definition: Only points of interest and routes with the status Active in the centralized catalogue maintained by Staff are used by itinerary planning, navigation, exploration and commercial booking; Inactive records are excluded from any new use.

details.title: Create Scheduling Request
details.definition: The Smart Scheduling Algorithm uses only points of interest and routes that are Active in the centralized catalogue maintained by Staff.

details.title: View Suggested Itinerary
details.definition: Only Active points of interest and Active routes are presented in an itinerary.

details.title: Explore Points of Interest
details.definition: Only Active points of interest of the centralized catalogue are returned.

details.title: Create Point of Interest
details.definition: Only a point of interest with the status Active is used by the itinerary planning and by the exploration functions.

details.title: Remove Point of Interest
details.definition: A point of interest with the status Inactive is no longer used by the itinerary planning, by the exploration and by the commercial booking functions.

details.title: Create Route
details.definition: Only a route with the status Active is used by the itinerary planning and by the navigation.

details.title: Update Route
details.definition: A route with the status Inactive is no longer used by the itinerary planning and by the navigation.

rules.definition: A generated itinerary must respect the opening hours of every scheduled point of interest and the estimated travel time between consecutive locations.

details.title: Create Scheduling Request
details.definition: A generated itinerary must respect the opening hours of every scheduled point of interest and the estimated travel time between consecutive locations.

details.title: View Suggested Itinerary
details.definition: A displayed itinerary must remain consistent with the opening hours and the estimated travel time of the scheduled locations.

details.title: Confirm Re-routing
details.definition: A proposed plan must respect the opening hours of the affected points of interest and the estimated travel time.

rules.definition: Itinerary versioning: every generated itinerary is stored with a version number starting at 1; each regeneration or manual adjustment creates a new version and only the Active version is the current plan. Parameter changes and offline synchronisation never create or alter versions.

details.title: Create Scheduling Request
details.definition: Every generated itinerary is stored with a version number; the first generated itinerary of a scheduling request is version 1.

details.title: View Suggested Itinerary
details.definition: A regeneration or a manual adjustment creates a new itinerary version; the version number is incremented.

details.title: Confirm Re-routing
details.definition: An accepted re-routing creates a new itinerary version with an incremented version number.

details.title: Configure Algorithm Parameters
details.definition: A change of the scheduling parameters never alters the already generated itinerary versions; it applies to the subsequent generations only.

details.title: View Active Trip Details
details.definition: Only the Active itinerary version is presented as the current plan; the superseded versions are listed as history only.

details.title: Synchronize Offline Trip Data
details.definition: The synchronisation never creates a new itinerary version; it applies the captured execution data to the existing Active version.

rules.definition: Superseded versions are retained as history and a previously published version may be restored; a later change to routes or other master data does not modify existing itinerary versions.

details.title: View Suggested Itinerary
details.definition: A previous itinerary version is retained and is never overwritten.

details.title: Confirm Re-routing
details.definition: The itinerary version in force before the re-routing is retained and is never overwritten.

details.title: Update Route
details.definition: The existing itinerary versions that already reference the route remain unchanged; the change affects the subsequent planning only.

details.title: Update Landing Page Content
details.definition: A previously published version is retained as history and may be restored as the published version.

rules.definition: Navigation requires an itinerary in the Active status and a granted device location permission.

details.title: Navigate Route
details.definition: Navigation requires an itinerary in the Active status and a granted device location permission.

rules.definition: An alert belongs to exactly one of the supported alert types: weather, traffic, point of interest closure and safety notice.

details.title: Receive Real-Time Alerts
details.definition: An alert belongs to exactly one of the supported alert types: weather, traffic, point of interest closure and safety notice.

rules.definition: An alert is delivered only to a Traveler whose Active itinerary or current position is affected by the detected condition.

details.title: Receive Real-Time Alerts
details.definition: An alert is delivered only to a Traveler whose Active itinerary or current position is affected by the detected condition.

rules.definition: A deviation beyond the configured threshold raises a re-routing suggestion; the suggestion is handled by UC-15 and is never applied automatically.

details.title: Navigate Route
details.definition: A deviation beyond the configured threshold raises a re-routing suggestion; the suggestion is handled by UC-15 and is never applied automatically.

details.title: Receive Real-Time Alerts
details.definition: An alert that affects the planned route raises a re-routing suggestion; the suggestion is never applied automatically.

details.title: Confirm Re-routing
details.definition: A re-routing suggestion is raised by a route deviation beyond the configured threshold or by an alert that affects the planned route.

rules.definition: Alerts raised during a trip are retained on the trip until it is completed, even after being dismissed from the banner, and open alerts are counted for monitoring.

details.title: Receive Real-Time Alerts
details.definition: An alert is retained in the Alerts list of the trip until the trip is completed, even after it has been dismissed from the banner.

details.title: View Active Trips
details.definition: The alerts raised during a trip remain retained on the trip and are counted in the Open Alerts column.

details.title: View Active Trip Details
details.definition: The alerts raised during the trip are presented with their type and their timestamp.

rules.definition: A re-routing is applied only after the explicit confirmation of the Traveler; a declined or an expired suggestion never changes the itinerary.

details.title: Confirm Re-routing
details.definition: A re-routing is applied only after the explicit confirmation of the Traveler; a declined or an expired suggestion never changes the itinerary.

details.title: Explore Points of Interest
details.definition: The details of a point of interest are presented only while the point of interest remains Active.

details.title: View Commercial Service
details.definition: The detailed information of a point of interest is displayed only while the point of interest has the status Active.

rules.definition: The turn-by-turn guidance of a route is obtained from the integrated map service; the stored route holds the distance, the estimated travel time and the transport mode.

details.title: Create Route
details.definition: The turn-by-turn guidance of a route is obtained from the integrated map service; the stored route holds the distance, the estimated travel time and the transport mode.

rules.definition: The offline data of an itinerary covers the itinerary items, the related points of interest, the route information and the map data of the itinerary area only.

details.title: Download Offline Map & Itinerary
details.definition: The offline data of an itinerary covers the itinerary items, the related points of interest, the route information and the map data of the itinerary area only.

rules.definition: The offline package of an itinerary must not exceed the configured storage limit of 150 MB; storage released after a successful synchronisation returns to this budget.

details.title: Download Offline Map & Itinerary
details.definition: The downloaded offline package must not exceed the configured storage limit of 150 MB.

details.title: Synchronize Offline Trip Data
details.definition: The local storage released after a successful synchronisation is returned to the 150 MB offline budget.

rules.definition: Offline data is handled as complete units: an itinerary is available offline only after every component has been stored, and a local record is uploaded only as a complete unit; partial data is never treated as complete.

details.title: Download Offline Map & Itinerary
details.definition: An itinerary is marked as available offline only after every required component has been stored successfully; an incomplete download is never treated as a completed offline package.

details.title: Synchronize Offline Trip Data
details.definition: A local record is uploaded only as a complete unit; a partially captured record is rejected and reported.

rules.definition: Every offline itinerary copy and local record carries its version and capture timestamp, which are used to detect superseded copies and synchronisation conflicts.

details.title: Download Offline Map & Itinerary
details.definition: The downloaded itinerary version is tracked locally, so that a superseded offline copy can be identified when the connectivity returns.

details.title: Synchronize Offline Trip Data
details.definition: Every local record carries its local version and its capture timestamp, which are the basis of the conflict detection.

rules.definition: Functions that require server confirmation (booking, payment, check-in) are never executed offline; offline navigation uses the data downloaded under UC-16.

details.title: Navigate Route
details.definition: While the device is offline, navigation uses the downloaded offline data of UC-16 and the functions that require server confirmation remain unavailable.

details.title: Download Offline Map & Itinerary
details.definition: The offline availability does not extend to the functions that require server confirmation, such as booking, payment and check-in.

details.title: Synchronize Offline Trip Data
details.definition: A function that requires a server confirmation, such as a booking or a payment, is never executed offline, therefore no such operation is part of the synchronised data.

details.definition: The Traveler who creates a travel group is automatically assigned as the Group Host.

details.definition: An invitation code must be unique across the system and must reference exactly one travel group.

details.definition: Only the Group Host may remove an active member from the travel group; the Group Host cannot remove itself through this function.

details.title: Invite Group Members
details.definition: An invitation may be used only while it is valid, unexpired and its travel group is available; generating or sharing an invitation never creates a membership.

details.title: Join Shared Group Trip
details.definition: A Traveler may hold at most one active membership in the same travel group at any time.

details.title: Create Travel Group
details.definition: A travel group containing active members must always have exactly one Group Host.

details.title: View Group Members
details.definition: A travel group containing active members always has exactly one Group Host, who is identified in the member list.

details.title: Remove Group Member
details.definition: A travel group containing active members always has exactly one Group Host; the removal must never leave the group without a Group Host.

details.title: Leave Travel Group
details.definition: A travel group containing active members must always have exactly one Group Host.

details.title: Join Shared Group Trip

details.definition: The GPS location of a group member is shared only when the member has explicitly opted in and the device location permission is granted; either condition alone is not sufficient.

details.definition: The availability of each departure schedule presented on this screen is retrieved at display time, and the presented availability is not a reservation.

Every list screen paginates at 20 records per page by default, states the total record count, and preserves the current page, applied filters and sort order when the user returns from a detail screen.

Every list screen that supports search applies the search on submit, not on each keystroke, and shows an explicit empty-result state using MSG33 for the POI catalogue, MSG64 for the tour catalogue and MSG128 for every other list, rather than an empty table.

Every input field is validated on the client for presence, length and format, and is validated again on the server before the request is accepted. A client-side pass never substitutes for the server-side check.

Required-field, length and format errors are displayed inline beneath the field using MSG01 for a missing required field and the field-specific message otherwise, for example MSG02, MSG04, MSG05, MSG06, MSG29, MSG118 or MSG123; they are never displayed only as a toast.

Every irreversible action — delete, deactivate, cancel, lock, reject — is confirmed through a modal using the confirmation message defined for that action, for example MSG59, MSG61, MSG81, MSG170 or MSG194, or MSG130 where the action has no confirmation message of its own, before the request is sent.

Every create, update and delete action that succeeds reports success through a toast using the success message defined for that action, for example MSG20, MSG54, MSG60, MSG82, MSG109, MSG112 or MSG191, or MSG129 where the action has no success message of its own, and leaves the user on a screen that reflects the new state.
Dates are displayed as dd/MM/yyyy and times as HH:mm in 24-hour form, in the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh time zone. All timestamps are stored in UTC and converted for display.
Monetary amounts are displayed in Vietnamese dong with a thousands separator and no decimal places, and are stored as an integer number of dong.
The user interface language is English for this version. All user-facing text comes from a resource file so that a Vietnamese locale can be added without code changes.
An expired session redirects the user to sign-in using MSG125, preserves the intended destination, and returns the user there after a successful sign-in.

A request for a screen or action outside the signed-in role’s permission is refused by the server and reported using MSG126, or using MSG84 where a Tour Operator requests booking data belonging to another Tour Operator, regardless of whether the client had hidden the entry point.

A network or server failure is reported using MSG127, using MSG89 where the failure is a payment gateway timeout and MSG106 where it interrupts an offline package download, and leaves the client state unchanged; the client never reports success it has not received.

Every write operation is idempotent against accidental double submission: the submit control is disabled while a request is in flight, and the server rejects a repeated submission of the same operation identifier, as MSG88 does for a repeated payment of the same booking.

Every administrative write action — account lock and unlock, application decision, tour decision, master data change, parameter change, refund-return receipt, failed-payout resolution — writes an audit record per BR-174 and section 3.1.4 item 10, confirmed to the Administrator using MSG119.
No screen displays another user’s personal data beyond what its use case requires, and no screen displays a full payment instrument number, a password or a token value.
